title: Asbestos schools (AHERA): response actions, O&M, management plans and records practice questions
description: Practice questions on AHERA school rules: response actions, clearance, O&M, fiber releases, training, management plans, records, labels (40 CFR 763).

questions.question: Damaged thermal system insulation ACM is present in a school building. Under 763.90(b), when must the local education agency remove the damaged material rather than repair it?

options.A: When repairing it would cost more than removing it
options.B: When it is not feasible, due to technological factors, to repair the damage
options.C: When students occupy the functional space during the school day
options.D: When the damaged area is larger than the undamaged area

questions.explanation: For damaged or significantly damaged thermal system insulation ACM, the local education agency shall "At least repair the damaged area" and "Remove the damaged material if it is not feasible, due to technological factors, to repair the damage."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 763.90, Response actions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Damaged friable surfacing ACM is present. Several response actions would protect human health and the environment. Under 763.90(c)(2), what may the local education agency then consider to decide which of them is least burdensome?

options.A: Only the recommendation of the abatement contractor
options.B: Only the age of the school building
options.C: Only the number of complaints from parents
options.D: Local circumstances, including occupancy and use patterns within the school building, and its economic concerns

questions.explanation: For determining which response actions are least burdensome, "the local education agency may then consider local circumstances, including occupancy and use patterns within the school building, and its economic concerns".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 763.90, Response actions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Significantly damaged friable miscellaneous ACM is found in a classroom. Under 763.90(d)(1), what must the local education agency do with the functional space?

options.A: Immediately isolate the functional space and restrict access, unless isolation is not necessary to protect human health and the environment
options.B: Keep the space in use and add it to the next periodic surveillance
options.C: Post a warning label and keep normal use until the next reinspection
options.D: Close the space only after the State has approved a response action

questions.explanation: If significantly damaged friable surfacing or miscellaneous ACM is present, the local education agency shall "Immediately isolate the functional space and restrict access, unless isolation is not necessary to protect human health and the environment."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 763.90, Response actions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Friable surfacing ACM in a gym has potential for significant damage. Under 763.90(f), what must the local education agency do in addition to implementing an O&M program?

options.A: Encapsulate the material within 30 days
options.B: Have the material reinspected every month
options.C: Institute preventive measures appropriate to eliminate the reasonable likelihood that the ACM or its covering will become significantly damaged, deteriorated, or delaminated
options.D: Notify the EPA Regional Office before the next school year

questions.explanation: Besides an O&M program, the local education agency shall "Institute preventive measures appropriate to eliminate the reasonable likelihood that the ACM or its covering will become significantly damaged, deteriorated, or delaminated."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 763.90, Response actions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A crew has finished enclosing ACBM in a school. Under 763.90(i)(1), who must visually inspect each functional space where the action was conducted?

options.A: An inspector from the EPA Regional Office
options.B: The laboratory that analyzes the clearance air samples
options.C: A person designated by the local education agency
options.D: The Agency designated by the Governor

questions.explanation: At the conclusion of any action to remove, encapsulate, or enclose ACBM, "a person designated by the local education agency shall visually inspect each functional space where such action was conducted to determine whether the action has been properly completed."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 763.90, Response actions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A local education agency is having clearance air samples analyzed by phase contrast microscopy (PCM), under circumstances 763.90 permits. Under 763.90(i)(2)(ii), which laboratories must it use for that PCM analysis?

options.A: Laboratories enrolled in the American Industrial Hygiene Association Proficiency Analytical Testing Program for PCM
options.B: Any laboratory the abatement contractor selects
options.C: Laboratories approved by the Agency designated by the Governor
options.D: The local health department's laboratory, whatever its enrollment

questions.explanation: Local education agencies shall have the air samples analyzed "using laboratories accredited by the National Bureau of Standards to conduct such analysis using transmission electron microscopy (TEM) or, under circumstances permitted in this section, laboratories enrolled in the American Industrial Hygiene Association Proficiency Analytical Testing Program for phase contrast microscopy (PCM)."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 763.90, Response actions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A local education agency will remove contiguous ACBM in one school building at the same time and wants to split it into smaller projects so each can be cleared by PCM under 763.90(i)(5). What does 763.90(i)(6) say?

options.A: Each project may be cleared by PCM if a separate contractor does it
options.B: Contiguous portions may be split if the projects start on different days of the same week
options.C: Splitting is allowed if the EPA Regional Office is told in writing
options.D: Contiguous portions of material subject to such action conducted concurrently or at approximately the same time within the same school building shall not be separated to qualify

questions.explanation: 763.90(i)(6) states: "Contiguous portions of material subject to such action conducted concurrently or at approximately the same time within the same school building shall not be separated to qualify under paragraph (i)(5)".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 763.90, Response actions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Nonfriable ACBM in a school will be disturbed by planned work so that it is about to become friable. How does 763.91(a) treat this material for the purposes of the O&M section?

options.A: It stays nonfriable ACBM until it is actually damaged
options.B: It must be treated as friable ACBM
options.C: It is treated as suspected ACBM that is not assumed to be ACM
options.D: It is excluded from the O&M program

questions.explanation: 763.91(a) says nonfriable ACBM or nonfriable assumed ACBM "must be treated as friable ACBM for purposes of this section when the material is about to become friable as a result of activities performed in the school building."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 763.91, Operations and maintenance (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 763.91(c)(2), who makes a written recommendation to the local education agency on whether additional cleaning is needed?

options.A: The accredited management planner
options.B: The custodial supervisor
options.C: The laboratory that analyzed the bulk samples
options.D: The Agency designated by the Governor

questions.explanation: "The accredited management planner shall make a written recommendation to the local education agency whether additional cleaning is needed, and if so, the methods and frequency of such cleaning."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 763.91, Operations and maintenance (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: During an O&M activity disturbing friable ACBM, how does 763.91(d)(1) say entry into the area by persons other than those necessary to perform the project is restricted?

options.A: Only by building a full plastic containment around the area
options.B: Only by locking the school building
options.C: Either by physically isolating the area or by scheduling
options.D: By asking the persons to sign a waiver

questions.explanation: The local education agency must "Restrict entry into the area by persons other than those necessary to perform the maintenance project, either by physically isolating the area or by scheduling."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 763.91, Operations and maintenance (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: About 5 square feet of friable ACBM falls from a school hallway ceiling, a major fiber release episode. Under 763.91(f)(2)(ii), what must be done with the building's air-handling system?

options.A: Leave it running normally until the next periodic surveillance
options.B: Increase its airflow to blow the fibers out of the area
options.C: Leave it unchanged and clean its filters after the response action
options.D: Shut it off or temporarily modify it to prevent the distribution of fibers to other areas in the building

questions.explanation: For a major fiber release episode ("more than 3 square or linear feet of friable ACBM"), the local education agency shall ensure the procedure to "Shut off or temporarily modify the air-handling system to prevent the distribution of fibers to other areas in the building" is followed.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 763.91, Operations and maintenance (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A minor fiber release episode has been cleaned up and the debris placed in a sealed, leak-tight container. Under 763.91(f)(1)(iv), what must then be done with the area of damaged ACM?

options.A: Leave it unrepaired until the next reinspection
options.B: Repair it with materials such as asbestos-free spackling, plaster, cement, or insulation, or seal it with latex paint or an encapsulant, or immediately have the appropriate response action implemented
options.C: Cover it with a sign and keep normal use with no repair
options.D: Record the episode and take no further action

questions.explanation: The procedures include: "Repair the area of damaged ACM with materials such as asbestos-free spackling, plaster, cement, or insulation, or seal with latex paint or an encapsulant, or immediately have the appropriate response action implemented as required by § 763.90."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 763.91, Operations and maintenance (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A school plumber never works with ACBM but may work in a building that contains it. Under 763.92(a)(1), does the awareness training requirement cover this plumber?

options.A: Yes, the requirement covers staff who may work in a building that contains ACBM, whether or not they are required to work with ACBM
options.B: No, it covers only staff who disturb ACBM
options.C: No, it covers only custodians, not trades staff
options.D: Only if the plumber was hired after the management plan was written

questions.explanation: Awareness training covers "all members of its maintenance and custodial staff (custodians, electricians, heating/air conditioning engineers, plumbers, etc.) who may work in a building that contains ACBM", "whether or not they are required to work with ACBM."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 763.92, Training and periodic surveillance (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 763.92(b)(2), what must each person performing periodic surveillance record?

options.A: Only the number of rooms entered
options.B: Air sample results for each functional space
options.C: The date of the surveillance, his or her name, and any changes in the condition of the materials
options.D: The names of the students in each room

questions.explanation: Each person performing periodic surveillance shall "Record the date of the surveillance, his or her name, and any changes in the condition of the materials."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 763.92, Training and periodic surveillance (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 763.93(i), who must sign the statement in each management plan certifying that the general local education agency responsibilities in 763.84 have been met or will be met?

options.A: The individual designated by the local education agency under 763.84
options.B: The laboratory that analyzed the bulk samples
options.C: An official of the EPA Regional Office
options.D: The abatement contractor that performed the latest response action

questions.explanation: "Each management plan must contain a true and correct statement, signed by the individual designated by the local education agency under § 763.84, which certifies that the general, local education agency responsibilities, as stipulated by § 763.84, have been met or will be met."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 763.93, Management plans (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A local education agency requires its management plans to contain a signed compliance statement under 763.93(f). What does 763.93(f) say about who signs it?

options.A: It must be signed by the principal of each school
options.B: It must be signed by an official of the EPA Regional Office
options.C: It must be signed by the chair of the school board
options.D: It may not be signed by a person who, in addition to preparing or assisting in preparing the plan, also implements (or will implement) it

questions.explanation: Under 763.93(f) the statement is "signed by an accredited management plan developer", and it "may not be signed by a person who, in addition to preparing or assisting in preparing the management plan, also implements (or will implement) the management plan."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 763.93, Management plans (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 763.93(g)(3), when must a school's management plan be available for inspection, without cost or restriction, to workers?

options.A: Only during the summer break
options.B: Before work begins in any area of a school building
options.C: Within 30 days after the work ends
options.D: Only after the Governor has approved the plan

questions.explanation: "Management plans shall be available for inspection, without cost or restriction, to workers before work begins in any area of a school building."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 763.93, Management plans (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A school district keeps the records that 763.94 requires, such as training, periodic surveillance, cleaning and O&M records. Under 763.94(a), where must those records be maintained?

options.A: Only at the office of the accredited contractor that did the most recent response action
options.B: Only in the administrative office of the school
options.C: In a centralized location in the administrative office of both the school and the local education agency, as part of the management plan
options.D: At the EPA Regional Office

questions.explanation: 763.94(a) says "Records required under this section shall be maintained in a centralized location in the administrative office of both the school and the local education agency as part of the management plan."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 763.94, Recordkeeping (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A school is preparing the warning labels it must attach next to ACBM left in place in its boiler room. What does 763.95(c) say about the print on the label?

options.A: It must be printed in the school's own colors
options.B: It must be handwritten by the person designated under 763.84
options.C: It must be the same size as the print in the management plan
options.D: It must be readily visible because of large size or bright color

questions.explanation: 763.95(c) says "The warning label shall read, in print which is readily visible because of large size or bright color, as follows", followed by the required caution wording.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 763.95, Warning labels (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 763.99(a)(6), an accredited inspector determines that no ACBM is present in a school area where asbestos removal operations were conducted before December 14, 1987. On what must that determination be based?

options.A: A letter from the school principal
options.B: Inspection records and contractor and clearance records
options.C: The original construction bid documents only
options.D: Interviews with the custodial staff

questions.explanation: The exclusion applies where, "Based on inspection records and contractor and clearance records, an accredited inspector has determined that no ACBM is present in the homogeneous or sampling area where asbestos removal operations have been conducted before December 14, 1987".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 763.99, Exclusions (as of Nov 4, 2026)
